chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Halabi from 'Ubayd Allah al-Halabi from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"There is no objection to delaying the Maghrib prayer during travel until the twilight (shafaq) disappears, and there is no objection to hastening the 'Atamah (Isha) prayer during travel before the twilight disappears."

key_terms.الشَّفَق: Twilight (the reddish glow in the sky after sunset)
key_terms.الْعَتَمَة: Isha prayer (often referred to as 'Atamah in hadith literature)

ai.seo_question: What are the permissible prayer time adjustments for travelers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific mechanism of *Jam' al-Taqdim* (early combination) for travelers, allowing Isha to be prayed before the full disappearance of twilight (*shafaq*) while Maghrib is delayed until then. This flexibility addresses the practical needs of travel, ensuring that the distinct times of the two prayers are maintained even when performed in a single sitting, a ruling widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence as a concession (*rukhsah*) for those on a journey.
